findings.title: Warden-down (DirectCdpBroker) attribution closes an innocent popup; the real dialog stays stuck
findings.severity: major (degraded mode only: the warden must be down while a dialog is open)
findings.rate: warden-down-opener-alerts 3/3 innocent popup closed then dead end; warden-down-chain-middle-alerts 3/3 innocent leaf closed first; warden-down-older-sibling-alerts 1/3 innocent newer sibling closed first; warden-down-newer-sibling-alerts 0/3 (correct)
findings.detail: In Direct mode nothing is tracked, so every dialog -- including one on the original tab or a middle popup -- is 'unknown' and attributeDialogHolders applies 'the newest leaf holds it'. That premise is only valid when the warden tracked every older target (then an unobserved dialog can only be in the newest target of a blocked renderer). With the warden down it is wrong for any dialog not in the newest leaf: `dialog accept` closes the innocent leaf; for an opener-held dialog it then finds the opener 'isolated' and refuses (exit 1), snap exit 3, only `close` escapes. Direct mode also has no discoveredAt, so sibling order falls back to targets() order.

findings.title: GAP-240 not fixed for the sibling shape: manual `dialog accept` closes a healthy popup during a sync-XHR false block
findings.rate: 3/3 (xhr-popup-manual); automatic policy 0/6 closes (xhr-popup-policy: exit 3 both --dialog accept and dismiss); isolated shape 0/6 closes
findings.detail: Opener O has a same-renderer popup P0 (no dialog anywhere). O runs a 15 s synchronous XHR. The gate reports two 'unknown' dialogs (O blockedBy P0). Following the hint, `sutradhar dialog accept` prints 'Tab <P0> (about:blank) was closed because its dialog could not be addressed directly' -- P0 had no dialog and was healthy; O stays blocked, the next accept refuses as isolated (exit 1) and snap exits 3 until the XHR finishes. The attribution treats 'opener + child both blocked' as evidence the child holds a dialog, but a busy opener produces exactly the same observation. The hint text ('never a different, healthy tab it merely shares a browser process with') is false here. The brief's check 3 ('neither automatic nor manual ever closes a target during a false block, isolated or with a sibling') fails on the manual+sibling cell. Heavy-layout variant (12 s forced-layout loop) did not reproduce (warden saw nothing blocked at probe time, 0/3).

findings.title: Real dialogs in a new tab that alerts during load are unrecoverable except `close` (fix-3's 'isolated' rule strands them)
findings.rate: pure CLI (no observer): target=_blank link -> page alerts while parsing: same-origin implicit-noopener 3/3 dead end, cross-site 2/3 dead end (1/3 the warden caught the event and it worked perfectly); rel=opener same-origin 0/3 (recovered via sibling rule). Observer probe: noopener same-origin 3/3, noopener cross-site 3/3, opener cross-site 3/3 dead end.
findings.detail: The warden usually misses a dialog fired during a new target's first parse (GAP-220's shape), so liveness reports it as 'unknown'. When the new tab has its own renderer (every target=_blank link since Chrome 88 is implicitly noopener; any cross-site popup), it has no blocked sibling, so fix-3 classifies it 'isolated' and refuses recovery under every path: `dialog accept` exit 1 and `dialog dismiss` exit 1 (message: 'nothing identifies this as an actual dialog (it may just be running a slow script)'), `snap --dialog accept` exit 3, `tabs` exit 3, every command exit 3. Only `close` (ending the whole session) escapes. This is GAP-230's dead end returning for the most common real-dialog-unknown shape; fix-2 recovered it by closing that tab. It is the direct cost of the GAP-240 isolated rule, and the message misdescribes a real alert as a possible slow script.

findings.title: Phantom and indistinguishable 'unknown' lines (GAP-244 residual)
findings.detail: (a) `dialog accept` prints the PRE-handle list as 'still pending' dialogPending lines: K=40 prints 40 stale 'unknown' lines after 'Accepted alert', although nothing is pending (a following `dialog accept` says 'no dialog is open'). (b) `sutradhar dialog` and the exit-3 lines give no target id and no holder/collateral marker, so an agent sees N identical 'unknown' lines and cannot tell which tab `dialog accept` will close before it closes it. (c) The warden's 409 redirect text tells the user to 'target that tab instead', but no CLI syntax targets a specific tab for `dialog accept|dismiss`.

notes: orphan (popup sync-alerts, opener then closed at browser level): 3/3 the popup is 'isolated' -> dialog accept refuses (exit 1), snap exit 3; only `close` escapes. Fail-safe (no wrong close, no hang). Not reachable through CLI verbs alone (every verb that could close the opener is gated). Accepted-trade territory (decision 6).

Chrome allows one popup per user activation: two open('') in one task yields one popup; multi-popup shapes need separate activations. Consequence: with the warden alive, a synchronous (untracked) dialog can only be in the NEWEST target of its renderer -- nothing in a blocked renderer can create a newer target -- which is why the newest-leaf rule holds whenever the warden is up.
The click on a rel=opener link crashed once with the pre-existing GAP-235 'Requesting main frame too early!' (1/3), exit 1 after 'Clicked #sameopener'.

noopener: Target.opener()/openerId IS populated even for noopener popups (same-origin and cross-site), but those popups got their own renderer (opener stayed responsive), so the popup is the only blocked target and attribution classifies it 'isolated' -- no wrong close, but see A4-03.
debugger-paused (observer holds a Debugger.pause): snap hits the probe's 60 s cap -- identical in audit-3 and fix-3 runs, observer-induced, not FR2-04.
many-blocked: after accept, the CLI's active tab is a popup (kid?i=N) -- pre-existing popup-adoption behavior, not FR2-04.

attributionAnalysis.whyItHoldsWithWardenUp: Chrome grants one popup per user activation and a renderer blocked by a dialog cannot create a newer target, so an UNOBSERVED (synchronous-at-creation) dialog is always in the newest target of its renderer, and every older target was tracked (Page.enable) by the warden, so any dialog on it surfaces as a real typed event. Newest-leaf is therefore right for every real-dialog shape tried with the warden up: single blank popup, older+newer siblings, 3-target chain leaf, second same-site CLI tab, rapid popups 0-100 ms apart (6/6), same-origin URL popup. Tracked dialogs on an opener/middle/older sibling are selected correctly (real alert handled first) -- only phantom 'unknown' lines appear.
whereItBreaks: A4-02: the premise 'both blocked + opener relation => the child holds a dialog' is also produced by a BUSY opener (sync XHR) with any same-renderer popup -> manual dialog accept closes the healthy popup (3/3).

A4-03: a real unobserved dialog in a target with its own renderer (target=_blank links are implicitly noopener; cross-site popups) has no sibling, is classified isolated and can never be recovered except by `close` (5/6 pure CLI, 9/9 probe).
A4-01: with the warden down nothing is tracked, so dialogs on openers/middle nodes are misattributed to the newest leaf (opener 3/3, chain-middle 3/3, older sibling 1/3).
smallestFixDirection: Replace 'has a blocked sibling' as the evidence rule with a per-target history the warden already nearly has: a target whose Page.enable ACKed AND that was later observed responsive (one cheap Performance.getMetrics right after the ack) cannot hold an unobserved dialog -- any dialog there would have arrived as an event. Such a target is never a holder and never closable (fixes A4-02, keeps GAP-240 isolated safe).

Conversely a target that has been unresponsive since the warden first saw it (never observed responsive while enabled) IS eligible for tab-close recovery even when isolated (fixes A4-03; a new tab that is busy from birth is the only false-positive left and it is a just-opened tab).
DirectCdpBroker has no history: make it refuse destructive recovery entirely and say the warden is down / use `close` (fixes A4-01 safely), or respawn the warden before the dialog verb.

Optional structural improvement for A4-03: have the warden set its own raw Target.setAutoAttach({waitForDebuggerOnStart:true,flatten:true}) so new targets stay paused until its Page.enable is sent, turning load-time dialogs in new tabs into real typed events.
Add tests: warden-level discoveredAt ordering (A13), selectDialog skipping blockedBy (A20), and make verify's GAP230 case assert WHICH target was closed.
